# intrastate

> A Go CLI that makes workflow state transitions explicit, reviewable,
> and deterministic. A flow is authored once as a transition model — a
> TOML document of tags, rules, guards, and writes — and callers
> navigate it by asking the CLI rather than reimplementing the flow in
> a skill, script, or agent. Given the same model, state, tags, and
> recognized outcome, the answer is the same every time: one legal
> plan, or one typed refusal.

The binary is authoritative and self-describing. Prefer asking it over
reading any file here — a file is a snapshot, the binary is the build
you actually have:

```sh
intrastate --help-all      # every command's full reference
intrastate <cmd> --help-all
intrastate <cmd> --as=json # one terminal JSON envelope per run
```

If `intrastate` is not on PATH:

```sh
go install github.com/cwensel/intrastate/cmd/intrastate@latest
```

## Commands

- [`intrastate flow`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-flow): Drive a transition model from a skill
- [`intrastate flow init-state`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-flow-init-state): Seed owned state from the model's [initial] root
- [`intrastate flow next`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-flow-next): Report the candidate rules the supplied state can take
- [`intrastate flow read-state`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-flow-read-state): Report what the declared read accessors see
- [`intrastate flow resolve`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-flow-resolve): Map one recognized outcome to exactly one plan
- [`intrastate flow set-state`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-flow-set-state): Apply planned owned-tag writes, verified by read-back
- [`intrastate graph`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-graph): Export a model's normalized graph as a document
- [`intrastate lint`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-lint): Check a transition model against the graph invariants
- [`intrastate version`](docs/cli-reference.md#intrastate-version): Print build version, commit, and date

## Docs

- [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md): every command, flag, and
  extended body — generated from the command tree.
- [Model authoring](docs/model-authoring.md): how to author a
  transition model in TOML — the model class, a decision table's
  cells, and the escape row. Not derivable from the CLI surface.
- [Output contract](docs/cli-output-contract.md): worked JSON
  payloads and the rationale behind the envelope shape.
- [Examples](docs/examples.md): the models, drawn — state machines
  and decision tables from this repo and from a real consumer.
- [README](README.md): what it is, install, and a first invocation.

## Examples

- [markdown-review.toml](models/examples/markdown-review.toml): reads a
  Markdown status with sed, updates one line, and verifies it by read-back.
- [pricing-decision-table.toml](models/examples/pricing-decision-table.toml):
  a stateless decision table, a proved 2x2 of tier x region with no
  gap, overlap, or escape row.
- [release-grammar.toml](models/examples/release-grammar.toml): the
  full grammar surface in one model — every tag kind, guard operator,
  and accessor construct the docs snippets are copied from.
- [review-state-machine.toml](models/examples/review-state-machine.toml):
  a stateful review flow, draft to approved or rejected, with escape
  rows closing the uncovered cases.
- [routing-decision-table.toml](models/examples/routing-decision-table.toml):
  a decision table with a partitioned emit domain, routing severity x
  owner into named dispositions.
- [rdr.toml](models/rdr.toml): the model this repo's own
  decision-record workflow runs on — the RDR lifecycle, Stage 1
  through Stage 8.

## Optional

- [Decision records](docs/rdr/README.md): the locked design decisions
  behind the contracts above. History and rationale; the code is the
  source of truth.
- [Joint decision records](docs/jdr/README.md): decisions two or more
  sibling RDRs jointly own, hoisted to one normative home instead of
  restated in each.
- [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md): layout, the contract every verb
  follows, and the build targets.
